steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish; set aside.
Cook sausage, bell pepper, and onion in a medium skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until sausage is no longer pink; drain and transfer to the baking dish.
Stir in potatoes, and 1 1/2 cups cheese until well combined.
Stir milk, Bisquick, eggs, and pepper together in a bowl until well combined. Pour into baking dish.
Bake, uncovered, until a knife inserted in center comes out clean, 40 to 45 minutes.
Sprinkle with remaining 1/2 cup cheese. Continue to bake until cheese melts, 1 to 2 minutes more. Cool 5 minutes.

review.reviewBody: This is our traditional family Christmas breakfast. I can make it up the night before and put it in the oven Christmas morning while we are all opening gifts. Really good.

Made this for out of town company (12 people total) and it was a hit! Everyone loved it. Read reviews first, and left out green pepper. Only thing I would do differently is stir the black pepper in with the sausage mixture instead of the liquid mixture so that it doesn't tend to clump.

Have made this several times, making changes as I go. First time did just as written and it was too cake like. Next time, cut making mix in half and add extra egg...better. last time, still halved baking mix and extra 2 egg and mixed half remaining cheese with egg mixture, sat overnight, added remaining cheese last few minutes to brown.... PERFECT!

Served to a dozen friends - all gave 5 stars! Made it even easier! After reading other allstars ideas, I used 1 pkg each of Jimmy Dean original Crumbles sausage (9.6 oz already cooked), & Oscar Mayer fully cooked bacon(2.5 oz) which I crisped in MW & diced. Then used potatos O'Brian which already has onion & peppers in it. Kept cheese, bisquick & milk the same, but used 6 eggs & 1/2 c. sour cream. Assembled it night before - BIG success! Thanks to reviewers who came before me for their ideas!
I always play around with this receipe and just add what I have in the kitchen- i find this receipe is a bit better if you mix in a small amount of sour cream. Keeps it more moist.

Great recipe, but I had to be creative with the ingredients! I used bacon, cooked but not crispy. I had no frozen hash browns so I boiled some potatoes till still slightly hard and cut into small cubes, and used low-fat mozzarella instead of chedder. It still turned out super yummy!

I made this for after church and everyone loved it. However, it came out too brown on the top and bottom and at first I suspected the oven was too hot. Today I checked with an oven thermometer (our church kitchen has a huge, expensive, almost-brand-new, industrial, expensive, stainless steel range/oven--and did I mention expensive?) but it was on point. Next time I would check it after 25-30 minutes. It wasn't overdone to the point of being burned, but it definitely was in too long. I used a 13x9" glass baking dish; maybe I should have turned the oven down 25 degrees like you're supposed to do when baking a cake in a glass dish. I assembled it the night before and baked it at church during the service. The only modifications I made were to omit the bell pepper, which I abhor, and instead of putting cheese on the top I just put the extra inside the casserole. It was very good!

I tried this and will be making it for "make ahead" brunch while entertaining company. I agree with another reviewer, instead of using frozen potatoes or tater tots, it's a bit more sophisticated with real potatoes. I finely and evenly chopped a couple cups of baby potatoes and pan cooked with butter and dried Italian seasoning. I did a side by side comparison in my pan. An extra step, but worth it. I also let it sit in the frig for a few hours to come together. A great dish to make the night before! I added yellow peppers...could use any veg you have I would imagine. I loaded it with shredded cheddar for flavor. Not low cal, but will be a crowd pleaser.

I made this for Christmas brunch this year and it was a hit. I did leave out the green peppers just to appease kids and adults both, but I think it would be good with them also. The sausage and onions were cooked the night before to save time. Put the rest together in the morning, baked and took it to the in-laws. It was great and so easy.

This was great however I did use 6 eggs added some chopped cooked and drained spinach, used cheddar, mozzarella and grated fresh Parmesan cheese. I also added 3/4 cup sour cream to make it creamy. Potatoes O’Brian and sautéed onion and pepper In butter with garlic. I also used jimmy dean precooked Turkey Sausage crumbles 2 1/2 bags. All the rest kept the same. It was fabulous and will make it again!

This was really good. I fried the sausage and cut up russet potatoes in a cast iron skillet(deep one). Then I put the cheese on top and poured the batter on top of that in the skillet, and put that in the oven. One pan.
Want to try it very soon. Looks delicious

The flavor on this is fantastic. This was easily scaled down to make 2 servings, which I baked in a small oval ramekin. I tossed the potatoes with salt and pepper. I used the hot spicy breakfast sausage and browned the sausage crumbles until they developed some darker bits on it for flavor, and those onions started to disintegrate. I did add a few twists of salt to the peppers and onions as they cooked. I adore sausage potato breakfast casseroles and this one is very tasty, but it's soft and moist and too fluffy as compared to one without Bisquick. The frozen potatoes took on a mealy texture and were soft and melded into one with the egg and Bisquick. Not sure if I liked that aspect. It's the texture that's throwing me off. The flavor on this is soooo good though that I was able to eat most of my serving. I'd fix this again without the Bisquick as this was off the charts delicious. Do use a good quality cheddar as it makes a difference in the flavor. If I weren't so texture oriented, I'd have rated this higher as it had the best flavor.
Delicious! Followed the instructions exactly and did not find it "cakey" as a few others did. It was perfect and leftovers went quickly!

Made this for a holiday brunch and everyone really liked it. I too used the potatoes O’brien (full bag) and made it overnight. I used 2 pounds of chicken sausage and was told the casserole was delicious as it had a lot of meat. I only used 1/2 of the cheese and mixed it into the meat and potato. I used the 4 eggs called for and thought it was darn tasty.
Even my kiddo that doesn’t like scrambled eggs, loved this! For the potatoes, onion, and peppers, I just used most of a bag of frozen potatoes O’Brien.
The whole family enjoyed this recipe!
I substitued Pancake Mix for the bisquick. This made the casserole a bit sweeter and fluffier! Served this bake to nine highway workers! They absolutely loved it!
Every time my kids/grandkids come into town, I make this for Saturday morning brunch! It is so easy to make and delicious! Definitely a five-star recipe!
